findings.reason: the deliverable "Every test that builds a ledger uses a temporary cache root" is not achieved for the case the section was written from, and the gate designed to prove it passes over that case, so a node implementing §9 literally lands a guard that reports safety it does not provide.
findings.text: §9's cited leak includes an index keyed to `…/pytest-of-mcintos/.../entry-points0`, which tests/test_spa_crew_stylesheet.py:49-55 creates with `tmp_path_factory.mktemp("entry-points")` in a **module-scoped** fixture whose body calls `serve._render_spa_html("fixture")`; that path reaches `ledger.load` at reckon/serve.py:1029, which builds `_run_index_path` → `_store.cache_root("pick-input")`. A module-scoped fixture is set up before the function-scoped autouse `isolated_reckon_home` (tests/conftest.py:1160-1170), so at that moment neither `RECKON_HOME` nor the proposed per-test `XDG_CACHE_HOME` is set and the root resolves to the real `~/.cache/reckon` — the leak survives the fix. The guard is blind to it for the same reason: a session-scoped wrapper that "fails the session naming any test that resolved a root outside its own temporary directory" has no test to name for a resolution made during module-fixture setup, so it records nothing and passes. The declared negative control (remove the fixture, "the wrapper names the tests that resolved the real cache") cannot redden for this case either, because there is no test to name — the control cannot validate the guard against the very leak §9 cites.

findings.reason: the section names the wrong environment variable for its own headline case and leaves the permitted root undefined against an existing fixture's actual resolution, so the worker either implements a fixture that does not move the ledger index or a guard that fails the whole suite for reasons unrelated to the leak.
findings.text: §9 says pointing `XDG_CACHE_HOME` makes "every cache root reckon resolves, the ledger index and the picker caches among them" fall under the test's directory, but `cache_root` (reckon/_store.py:158-201) returns `_config_home()/cache/leaf` for the `pick-input` kind whenever `RECKON_HOME` is set, *before* it ever reads `XDG_CACHE_HOME` (the `home_order == "before"` branch for pick-input precedes the `XDG_CACHE_HOME` branch). The ledger index therefore does not follow `XDG_CACHE_HOME` at all; it follows the `RECKON_HOME` the existing fixture already sets to a `tmp_path_factory.mktemp("reckon-home")` directory. That directory is not the test's own `tmp_path`, so the same sentence is false on the other side too: a guard failing on any resolution "outside its own temporary directory" reddens on healthy ledger-building tests that resolve to `<basetemp>/reckon-home*/cache`.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — tests/conftest.py, tests/test_spa_crew_stylesheet.py, `_store.cache_root` (reckon/_store.py:158) and `RECKON_PICK_CACHE` (reckon/_store.py:172) all resolve, and the cited evidence and plan hrefs carry an explicit `.html`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §9's fix and its guard are both scoped to a running test, while the leak its own Why cites resolved outside any test.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the negative-control log and the gate write under the run directory on the all_debug partition, not a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §9 names no new symbol, file or comment carrying a plan label, stage name or ticket id.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the mechanism §9 prescribes (a per-test `XDG_CACHE_HOME`) cannot reach the resolution that produced the cited leak.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §9 carries one deliverable, keeping tests out of the real cache.
